x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Mission Vatsalya subsumed the Integrated Child Protection Scheme, not ICDS. Statement 3 is wrong: sponsorship/foster care support is ₹4,000 per child per month. Statement 4 is wrong: aftercare covers 18-21 years.

st.1: The certificate of identity is issued by the National Council for Transgender Persons.
st.2: The definition of a transgender person excludes persons with intersex variations.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the certificate of identity is issued by the District Magistrate. Statement 2 is wrong: the definition includes persons with intersex variations. Statement 4 is wrong: the Act provides no job reservation.

st.2: Gram Sabhas identify and free bonded labourers.
st.1: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Ordinance of 25 October 1975 preceded the Act of 1986.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Ordinance of 1975 was followed by the Act of 1976. Statement 2 is wrong: District Vigilance Committees identify and free bonded labourers. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2016 scheme is a Central Sector scheme with 100% Central funding.

st.1: PMKVY, launched in 2015 as the flagship of the Skill India Mission, has the Ministry of Labour and Employment as its nodal Ministry.
st.3: The National Skill Development Policy (2009) set a target of 500 million skilled workers by 2030.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the nodal Ministry of PMKVY is MSDE. Statement 2: SANKALP is supported by the World Bank, not the ADB. Statement 3: the 2009 policy's target of 500 million was for 2022.

st.3: SPMRM is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, while DILRMP is a Central Sector scheme.

x: All three statements are correct: PM-KISAN, PM Vishwakarma and DILRMP are Central Sector schemes, SPMRM is Centrally Sponsored, and CSS funding is 60:40, 90:10 for NE/Himalayan States and 100% for UTs without legislature.

st.4: India gets about 80% of the waters of the Indus system.
st.1: It was signed at New Delhi on 19 September 1960 by Nehru and Ayub Khan.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the treaty was signed at Karachi. Statement 3 is wrong: the eastern rivers went to India and the western rivers to Pakistan. Statement 4 is wrong: India gets about 20%; Pakistan gets about 80%.

st.2: Capacity building is the fourth C added to the Commerce, Culture and Connectivity framework of Act East.

x: All three statements are correct: countering China and new markets drove Look East, capacity building is the fourth C of Act East, and the North-East is the gateway to ASEAN.

st.1: Russia, a 20% shareholder of the New Development Bank, was expelled from the NDB in March 2022.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NDB only froze Russia-linked operations in March 2022; Russia was not expelled. Statement 2 is wrong: the 16th BRICS Summit (October 2024) was held at Kazan, Russia.

st.1: It was founded in 1949 and is headquartered at Brussels.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Council of Europe is headquartered at Strasbourg. Statement 2 is wrong: it is not a body of the European Union.

st.1: The 'Digital Single Market Strategy' is an initiative of the European Union.

x: All three statements are correct: the Digital Single Market Strategy (2015) is an EU initiative, the EU made commitments in 144 services subsectors under the India-EU FTA, and the Stability and Growth Pact limits budget deficits.

st.4: China is a member of the MTCR, though Pakistan is not.
st.1: The Australia Group controls missiles and drones that can carry 500 kg over 300 km.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it is the MTCR that controls such missiles and drones; the Australia Group deals with chemical and biological items. Statement 3 is wrong: the Wassenaar Arrangement is based at Vienna. Statement 4 is wrong: China and Pakistan are outside both the MTCR and Wassenaar.

st.1: The Leiden Plates were returned to India by the United Kingdom in May 2026.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: the Leiden Plates were returned by the Netherlands. Statement 2: the four Ds are Democracy, Demography, Demand and Diaspora, not Development.

st.2: Article 371D provides for a Central University in Andhra Pradesh.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Central University provision is Article 371E; Article 371D deals with equal opportunities in public employment and education. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 371J was inserted by the 98th Amendment.

st.2: It was passed as the 126th Constitution Amendment Bill.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 103rd Amendment was passed as the 124th Amendment Bill. Statement 4 is wrong: EWS reservation came with the 103rd Amendment; the 102nd created the NCBC.

st.3: If the innocent SC/ST member is executed as a result, the punishment is imprisonment for life.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: fabricating such evidence is punished with imprisonment for life and fine. Statement 3 is wrong: if the innocent person is executed, the punishment is death.

st.1: Article 324 provides for adult suffrage at 18 years.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: adult suffrage is in Article 326; Article 324 deals with the Election Commission. Statement 3 is wrong: Kuldip Nayar (2009) held voting to be a statutory right, not a Fundamental Right.

st.3: The National Plan of Action for Children, 2016 operationalised the National Policy for Children, 1974.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: under the 2013 policy a child is a person below 18 years. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2016 Plan of Action operationalised the National Policy for Children, 2013.

st.4: C.O. 272 of 5 August 2019 applied all provisions of the Constitution except Part IV to Jammu and Kashmir.
st.1: Ireland borrowed the idea of Directive Principles from the Soviet Constitution.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Ireland borrowed the idea from the Spanish Constitution. Statement 3 is wrong: under the 1954 Order neither Part IV nor Part IVA applied to J&K. Statement 4 is wrong: C.O. 272 applied all provisions, Part IV included.

st.1: Golaknath and Sajjan Singh held that an amendment is not 'law' under Article 13(2).

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it was Shankari Prasad and Sajjan Singh that held so; Golaknath held that an amendment is 'law'. Statement 3 is wrong: Kesavananda Bharati upheld the 24th Amendment.

st.4: As of November 2026, the latest enacted amendment is the 105th (2021).

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the procedure is partly rigid and partly flexible. Statement 4 is wrong: the latest enacted amendment is the 106th (2023).

st.1: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 was brought under Article 368.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Bill was brought under Article 3, not as a constitutional amendment under Article 368. Statement 3 is wrong: the Andhra State Bill received assent on 14 September 1953.

st.2: A member may give not more than two calling attention notices for a sitting.

x: All three statements are correct: calling attention was introduced in 1954, a member may give up to two notices for a sitting, and the device restricted the scope of the adjournment motion.

st.2: The Speaker's certificate that a Bill is a Money Bill is final under Article 199.

x: All three statements are correct: a Money Bill starts only in the Assembly on the Governor's recommendation, the Speaker's certificate is final under Article 199, and the Council must return it within 14 days.

st.3: Ambassadors are appointed by the President on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

x: All three statements are correct: after the 44th Amendment the President may return advice once, the appointment of the majority leader as PM rests on convention, and Ambassadors are appointed on ministerial advice.

st.3: M. Hidayatullah acted as President after President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed died in office.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: a President elected to fill a vacancy gets a full five-year term. Statement 3 is wrong: it was B.D. Jatti who acted in 1977; Hidayatullah acted in 1969 after Zakir Husain's death.

st.3: He may defend an accused person in a criminal prosecution even without the permission of the Government of India.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: he may defend an accused only with the Government's permission. Statement 4 is wrong: the Attorney General is not a full-time government servant and is not debarred from private practice.

st.3: Jammu and Kashmir was the first State to enact its own anti-defection law, in 1979.

x: All three statements are correct: the 52nd Amendment (in force 1 March 1985) amended Articles 101, 102, 190 and 191, and J&K had its own law in 1979.

st.3: The opinion tendered by the Court is not binding on the President.

x: All three statements are correct: the Court may refuse a reference under Article 143(1), must answer one under Article 143(2), and its opinion is advisory, not binding.

st.4: CESTAT hears income-tax and wealth-tax disputes.
st.3: Appeals from the National Sports Tribunal lie to the High Court.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: appeals from Debt Recovery Tribunals lie to the DRAT. Statement 3 is wrong: appeals from the National Sports Tribunal lie to the Supreme Court. Statement 4 is wrong: CESTAT hears customs, excise and service tax disputes; income tax goes to the ITAT.

st.2: The 17th Civil Services Day (2025) was the first at which PM's Awards for Excellence in Public Administration were given.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the first function in 2006 was held at Vigyan Bhawan. Statement 2 is wrong: the PM's Awards have been given since the early Civil Services Days; sixteen were given on the 17th Day (2025).

st.1: It was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948 in New York.
st.4: It consists of a Preamble and 30 articles and is a legally binding treaty.
st.2: The committee that drafted it was chaired by Rene Cassin.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the UDHR was adopted in Paris. Statement 2: the drafting committee was chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt; Rene Cassin was a principal drafter. Statement 3: resolution 423(V) fixing Human Rights Day was passed in 1950. Statement 4: the UDHR has a Preamble and 30 articles but is not a legally binding treaty.

st.1: In an inquiry it has the powers of a criminal court under the CrPC, such as summoning persons and requiring documents.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NHRC has the powers of a civil court under the CPC, 1908. Statement 3 is wrong: the Government must inform it of action taken within one month.

st.3: 'Public authority' under Section 2(h) excludes NGOs even if they are substantially financed by the government.
st.2: 'Information' under Section 2(f) includes records but excludes opinions and advices.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the right to inspect does not include taking files out of the office. Statement 2: 'information' includes e-mails, opinions, advices, logbooks, samples and models. Statement 3: 'public authority' includes NGOs substantially financed by the government.

st.4: UNCAC was adopted in 2003 at Palermo.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: UNODC is headquartered in Vienna. Statement 4 is wrong: UNCAC was adopted at Merida; Palermo is linked to UNTOC (2000).

st.3: It proposed a National Judicial Council.

x: All three statements are correct: the 2nd ARC's 15 reports are a reference for reforms, and it recommended a Code of Ethics, Right to Public Services laws, a Department of E-Governance and a National Judicial Council.

st.3: The Fifteenth Finance Commission cut the share to 41% because Telangana was carved out of Andhra Pradesh.
st.1: The Twelfth Finance Commission gave the States 32% of the divisible pool.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it was the Thirteenth Finance Commission that gave 32%. Statement 2 is wrong: the Fourteenth FC was chaired by Y.V. Reddy; N.K. Singh chaired the Fifteenth. Statement 3 is wrong: the cut to 41% was because Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory.

st.2: Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, the District Level Committee is the authority to initiate the process of determining individual and community forest rights.
st.1: The AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation 1 of 1959, amended by Regulation 1 of 1970, bars land transfers between tribals and non-tribals but allows them among non-tribals.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Regulation also bars transfers among non-tribals. Statement 2 is wrong: the Gram Sabha initiates the process. Statement 3 is wrong: OTFDs must show three generations (75 years) before 2005.

st.2: Until August 2026, Mayors in Andhra Pradesh were elected indirectly by the councillors.

x: All three statements are correct: the Third Amendment Bill introduced a Uniform Mutation Fee, Mayors were indirectly elected until the August 2026 decision for direct election, and GVMC has zonal commissioners.

st.2: Such proxy representation has no legal basis; the elected woman remains the office-holder.

x: All three statements are correct: in sarpanch-pati practice a male relative runs the office informally, it has no legal standing, and at Therku Thittai a Dalit woman president was made to sit on the floor.

st.1: The Government of India Act, 1919 made local self-government a reserved subject.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 1919 Act made local self-government a transferred subject. Statement 4 is wrong: the 1935 Act made it a provincial subject.

st.3: It functions under the Ministry of Finance.

x: All three statements are correct: the Department of Disinvestment was set up on 10 December 1999, renamed DIPAM on 14 April 2016, and it works under the Ministry of Finance.

st.3: The Bharatiya Kisan Union is the oldest agrarian pressure group.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana is based in Maharashtra. Statement 3 is wrong: the All India Kisan Sabha (1936) is the oldest agrarian pressure group.

st.2: Eco Mark for environment-friendly consumer products is issued by the Central Pollution Control Board.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Eco Mark (1991) is issued by the Bureau of Indian Standards. Statement 4 is wrong: hallmarking of gold became mandatory in June 2021.

st.2: It is based on credible minimum deterrence and first use against a large conventional attack.
st.1: It was adopted by the National Security Council on 4 January 2003.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the doctrine was adopted by the Cabinet Committee on Security. Statement 2 is wrong: it is based on No First Use. Statement 4 is wrong: the Executive Council is chaired by the National Security Adviser.

st.2: The rest of Waltair became the new Rayagada division of East Coast Railway.

x: All three statements are correct: the Andhra part of Waltair went to the Visakhapatnam division of SCoR, the rest became the Rayagada division of East Coast Railway, and Odisha claimed the K-K line.

st.4: As per SRS 2024, India's TFR has risen back above replacement level.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Andhra Pradesh's NFHS-5 TFR is 1.7. Statement 4 is wrong: India's TFR remains below replacement level.

st.2: Men accounted for 60.54% of the person-days.
st.1: AP ranked first nationally with 1,635.10 lakh person-days.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: AP ranked 3rd. Statement 2: women accounted for 60.54% of the person-days. Statement 3: the wage rate was ₹307 a day.

st.2: Stunting is low height-for-age and indicates chronic malnutrition.

x: All three statements are correct: wasting is low weight-for-height (acute), stunting is low height-for-age (chronic), and undernutrition with obesity is the double burden of malnutrition.

st.1: Manufacturing contributes more to GSDP than agriculture and allied sectors.
st.2: The Industrial Development Policy 4.0 covers the period 2020-25.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: manufacturing is only about 11% of GSDP, far below agriculture's share. Statement 2 is wrong: IDP 4.0 covers 2024-29. Statement 4 is wrong: AP's farm share is well above the national share.

st.3: Agriculture as a whole employed a smaller share of AP's workers than India's 54.6%.
st.1: Cultivators formed 24.7% of AP's workers, against 14.5% for India.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: cultivators were 14.5% in AP against 24.7% for India. Statement 3 is wrong: agriculture employed 62.4% of AP's workers, above India's 54.6%. Statement 4 is wrong: agricultural labourers outnumber cultivators by about 3.3:1.

st.4: The Kerala model shows that high human development is possible only at a high per capita income.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a large primary-sector share indicates underdevelopment. Statement 4 is wrong: the Kerala model shows high human development at a modest per capita income.

st.1: Its draft outline was presented by the Finance Ministry in July 1951.
st.3: About one-third of its outlay went to heavy industry, and it is associated with Bhakra Nangal and Hirakud.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the draft outline was presented by the Planning Commission. Statement 2: it was the First Plan that first proposed co-operative village management. Statement 3: about one-third of the outlay went to agriculture and irrigation.

st.1: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015 by a Union Cabinet resolution.

x: All three statements are correct: NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015 by a Cabinet resolution, the NDC's work has passed to the Governing Council, and the 11th Governing Council meeting asked for district-level GDP.

st.1: Stabilisation measures were long-term supply-side reforms.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: stabilisation was short-term demand management. Statement 3 is wrong: subsidy cuts, tight money and devaluation are stabilisation measures.

st.3: Decimal coinage was introduced from 1 April 1957 under the RBI Act, 1934.
st.1: The General Bank of Bengal and Bihar was set up in 1806.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the General Bank of Bengal and Bihar was set up in 1773. Statement 2: the 1899 Act placed India on the gold standard. Statement 3: decimal coinage came under the Indian Coinage (Amendment) Act, 1955.

st.3: In FY25 health insurance was the top non-life segment, ahead of motor.

x: All three statements are correct: IRDAI's vision is 'Insurance for All by 2047', FY25 premium income was Rs 11.9 lakh crore, and health has passed motor as the top non-life segment.

st.1: The RBI recognised MFIN and Sa-Dhan as self-regulatory organisations in 2014.

x: All three statements are correct: MFIN and Sa-Dhan became RBI-recognised SROs in 2014, the AP Ordinance of 2010 required MFIs to register with district authorities, and Malegam capped lenders per borrower at two.

st.1: It mainly serves tenant farmers and oral lessees.

x: All three statements are correct: NABARD's JLG scheme (2006) serves tenant farmers and oral lessees through groups of 4-10 members who give a mutual guarantee.

st.2: They were created directly under the RRB Act, 1976, without any earlier ordinance.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: RRBs were first created by an ordinance in 1975, later replaced by the RRB Act, 1976. Statement 3 is wrong: the shares are Centre 50, sponsor bank 35 and State 15.

st.2: The State Government holds a 50% share in Regional Rural Banks.
st.1: A Regional Rural Bank is sponsored by NABARD.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: an RRB is sponsored by a commercial bank. Statement 2: the Centre holds 50%; the State holds 15% and the sponsor bank 35%.

st.1: It proposed that the RBI hold the Government's stake in PSBs.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: P.J. Nayak proposed a Bank Investment Company to hold the stake. Statement 2: it recommended cutting the Government's stake below 50%.

st.1: The minimum default to trigger CIRP is ₹1 lakh.
st.2: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India votes on the resolution plan.
st.4: The Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process for MSMEs (2021) has a 180-day limit.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the minimum default is ₹1 crore. Statement 2: the Committee of Creditors votes on the resolution plan. Statement 3: the outer limit is 330 days. Statement 4: the pre-pack process has a 120-day limit.

st.3: Between May and 3 September 2013 the rupee rose by about 17% against the US dollar.
st.1: The East Asian financial crisis of 1997 began with the fall of the Indonesian rupiah.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the crisis began with the fall of the Thai baht. Statement 2: the taper tantrum was triggered by the US Federal Reserve. Statement 3: the rupee fell by about 17%.

st.2: NRI deposits were its largest component.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: commercial borrowings were the largest component. Statement 3 is wrong: the ADB was the largest multilateral lender.

st.1: It reached 8.4% of GDP in 1980-81.
st.2: In the 2020-21 COVID year it reached 7.3% of GDP, with a revenue deficit of 9.2%.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: the fiscal deficit reached 8.4% of GDP in 1990-91. Statement 2: in 2020-21 the fiscal deficit was 9.2% and the revenue deficit 7.3%.

st.4: When it is invoked, the Government need not place any justification before Parliament.
st.1: A routine shortfall in tax revenue is among its grounds.
st.2: It can be triggered when real output growth rises at least 3 percentage points above the average of the previous four quarters.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the grounds are national security, war, national calamity, collapse of agriculture and structural reforms, not a routine tax shortfall. Statement 2: it is triggered when growth falls 3 percentage points below the average. Statement 3: the deviation allowed is up to 0.5% of GDP. Statement 4: the Government must place a justification and a path back before Parliament.

st.1: It is Statement 21 of the Union Budget documents.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Gender Budget Statement is Statement 13. Statement 3 is wrong: Part A covers 100% schemes; Part C covers schemes with less than 30% for women.

st.3: The India-Japan bilateral swap, renewed from 28 February 2026, is a two-way arrangement in local currencies against US dollars.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: India became the fourth-largest holder by overtaking Russia, not Japan.

st.2: Special Rupee Vostro Accounts are rupee accounts of foreign banks maintained with Indian banks.

x: All three statements are correct: the RBI's rupee trade framework came in July 2022, SRVAs are foreign banks' rupee accounts with Indian banks, and surplus balances may go into corporate bonds and CPs.

st.4: The theme of the M.S. Swaminathan Centenary Conference (August 2025) was 'Doubling Farmers' Income'.
st.1: C. Subramaniam led the Green Revolution policy push as Union Finance Minister.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Subramaniam led the push as Union Minister for Food and Agriculture (1964-66). Statement 2 is wrong: Borlaug's HYVs were wheat varieties. Statement 4 is wrong: the theme was 'Evergreen Revolution, The Pathway to Biohappiness'.

st.1: Agriculture and allied growth was negative in 2002-03 and 2020-21.
st.2: The National Agricultural Policy 2000 set a growth target of over 6% per annum.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: agricultural growth was negative in 2002-03 and 2014-15; it stayed positive in 2020-21. Statement 2: the National Agricultural Policy 2000 set a target of over 4% a year.

st.2: The second advance estimate puts foodgrain production in 2025-26 below that of 2024-25.
st.1: Foodgrain production was 50.8 million tonnes in 1965-66.
st.4: Foodgrain production fell steadily from 2019-20 to 2024-25.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: 50.8 MT was the output of 1950-51. Statement 2: the 2nd AE of 376.56 MT for 2025-26 is a record, above 357.73 MT in 2024-25. Statement 3: horticulture has exceeded foodgrains every year since 2012-13. Statement 4: foodgrain output rose steadily over 2019-20 to 2024-25.

st.2: Annadata Sukhibhava - PM Kisan gives Rs 20,000 per family a year (AP Rs 6,000 + Centre Rs 14,000).

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the split is AP Rs 14,000 and Centre Rs 6,000. Statement 3 is wrong: YSR Rythu Bharosa gave Rs 13,500 per family a year.

st.1: Pesticide use fell from about 2,650 MT in 2014-15 to 1,716 MT in 2024-25.

x: All three statements are correct: pesticide use fell from 2,650 MT to 1,716 MT, fertiliser consumption was 39.39 LMT in 2024-25, and 2015-16 use was 80.78% of the allotment.

st.2: Post-harvest losses of foodgrains can be up to 40%, given a 30% cold-chain deficit.
st.4: About 86% of holdings are medium and large.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: losses of up to 40% refer to fruits and vegetables. Statement 3 is wrong: 10.9 : 4.1 : 1 is the skewed actual ratio; the ideal is 4 : 2 : 1. Statement 4 is wrong: about 86% of holdings are small and marginal.

st.1: Only about half of the agriculture target of the Annual Credit Plan 2025-26 was disbursed.
st.3: AP ranks third in SHG-Bank Linkage with about 36% of national disbursement.
st.4: PACS are being made Multi-Service Centres with SIDBI support.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: about 97% of the agriculture target was disbursed. Statement 2: AP's priority sector lending was 63.28% of ANBC. Statement 3: AP ranks first in SHG-Bank Linkage. Statement 4: PACS are being made Multi-Service Centres with NABARD support.

st.1: Farmers get a lower share for pulses than for perishables.
st.2: Gram gives farmers about 33% of the consumer rupee.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: farmers get a higher share for pulses than for perishables such as tomato (about 33%). Statement 2: gram gives farmers about 75% of the consumer rupee.

st.3: A Miniratna-I CPSE must have a pre-tax profit of ₹30 crore or more in each of the last three years.
st.4: Ratna CPSEs may depend on budgetary support or a Government guarantee.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a Navratna needs 60 or more marks. Statement 3 is wrong: the ₹30 crore pre-tax profit is needed in at least one of the three profit-making years. Statement 4 is wrong: no Ratna CPSE may depend on budgetary support or a Government guarantee.

st.3: It created District Industries Centres to give one-roof support to large industrial houses.
st.4: It eased the MRTP Act and FERA for large houses, after which IBM and Coca-Cola expanded in India.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the first strong export emphasis came with the 1980 Statement. Statement 3 is wrong: the DICs supported small and cottage industries. Statement 4 is wrong: the 1977 policy curbed large houses through MRTP and FERA, and IBM and Coca-Cola left India.

st.3: The composite investment-plus-turnover criterion was notified on 1 June 2020, effective 1 April 2021.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the MSMED Act came into force on 2 October 2006. Statement 3 is wrong: the composite criterion took effect on 1 July 2020.

st.1: It was done mainly to earn higher profits for the State.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: the State took over sick units mainly to protect jobs. Statement 2: the takeovers lowered the public sector's rate of return.

st.1: It was launched by NITI Aayog in 2016 with a target of 12% annual growth till 2029.
st.3: It targets an HDI of 0.9 by 2047 through the saturation approach.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Sunrise AP Vision 2029 is the AP Government's vision, not NITI Aayog's. Statement 2 is wrong: it aims to double per capita income every five years. Statement 3 is wrong: the HDI target of 0.9 is for 2029.

st.4: SES 2024-25 targets 30% agricultural growth over five years through 40 growth engines.
st.1: Foodgrain production peaked at 123.57 lakh tonnes in the drought year 2018-19.
st.3: Foodgrain output dipped to 108.39 lakh tonnes in 2019-20.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: the peak of 123.57 lakh t was in 2019-20. Statement 2: AP gives about 10% of India's farm output. Statement 3: the dip to 108.39 lakh t was in the drought year 2018-19. Statement 4: SES 2024-25 names 17 growth engines.

st.1: AP's foodgrain output in 2025-26 (2nd AE) is 109.29 lakh tonnes.
st.2: AP produces about 29% of India's fish and ranks second.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1: AP's 2025-26 foodgrain output (2nd AE) is 190.29 lakh tonnes. Statement 2: AP ranks first in fish. Statement 3: Rayalaseema, not North Coastal Andhra, is the Horticulture Hub.

st.1: Primary deficit is revenue deficit minus interest payments.
st.2: Since AP runs a primary deficit, its borrowing is used only to pay interest.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1: primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments. Statement 2: a primary deficit means borrowing also funds current spending beyond interest.

st.1: It is a lift irrigation scheme.

x: All three statements are correct: Pattiseema is a lift scheme with 24 pumps, a stop-gap until Polavaram's gravity flow starts.

st.1: Atchutapuram (APSEZ), the State's largest SEZ, is in Srikakulam district.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Atchutapuram is near Visakhapatnam, not in Srikakulam. Statement 2 is wrong: Sri City is a multi-product SEZ in Satyavedu and Varadaiahpalem mandals.

st.3: At present Tamil Nadu also has the largest number of approved SEZs.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Nandigram is in Purba Medinipur district. Statement 3 is wrong: Telangana has the most approved SEZs, while Tamil Nadu has the most operational ones.

st.3: In July 2026, AP signed an MoU with UN-Habitat for a Centre of Excellence for Urban Affairs in Amaravati, aligned with SDG 11.

x: All three statements are correct: AP's SDG framework is part of ROMS, APSDPS runs the Swarna Andhra @2047 dashboards, and the July 2026 MoU was with UN-Habitat.

st.1: It was prescribed by the RBI to replace the Business Responsibility Report (BRR).
